author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 바닷가 모래언덕, 섬과 강가의 농경지, 고원의 밭
summary: 국내에서는 2007년 10월 보령 소황사구에서 처음 기록된 뒤 지금까지 기록이 10건이 안 되는 길잃은새로, 늦가을부터 봄 사이에 바닷가 모래땅이나 섬·강가의 농경지, 고원의 밭에서 드물게 보였다. 유라시아와 북아메리카 북부의 툰드라와 고산, 초원에서 번식하고, 겨울에는 남쪽의 트인 땅과 바닷가로 옮겨 간다. 땅 위를 걸어 다니며 풀씨와 곤충을 먹고, 땅의 오목한 곳에 마른 풀로 둥지를 짓는다.

points.en: yellow forehead, supercilium, chin and throat
small black horn-like tufts at the crown sides (male)
black mask from the lores down onto the cheeks
black band across the upper breast

sexes.male: 이마와 멱이 노랗고, 정수리 앞쪽의 검은 띠와 양옆의 짧은 깃뿔, 눈 밑으로 휘는 검은 얼굴 무늬와 가슴의 검은 띠가 뚜렷하다.
sexes.female: 깃뿔이 짧고 머리의 검은 부분이 좁고 흐리며, 이마와 멱의 노란색이 칙칙하고 윗면의 세로무늬가 더 짙다.

young: 어린새는 머리와 가슴의 검은 무늬가 없고, 흑갈색 윗면에 노르스름한 흰 점이 촘촘히 박혀 얼룩덜룩하며 가슴도 거무스름한 얼룩으로 덮인다. 8월에 깃갈이를 마치므로 겨울에 오는 새는 어른새와 비슷하다.

art.subject: Horned Lark (Eremophila alpestris), adult male in winter of the yellow-faced northern form (flava) seen in Korea from November to March: forehead, broad supercilium and throat pale yellow; a black band across the forecrown ending in two short black feather tufts ('horns') at the rear sides of the crown, partly veiled by pale feather tips in winter; a broad black mask from the bill base through the lores, curving down below the eye onto the cheek; a broad black crescent across the upper breast, separated from the mask by yellow; crown and nape grey-brown with a faint pinkish-cinnamon tinge; mantle and wing coverts sandy grey-brown with diffuse dark streaks; rest of the underparts white, with a grey-brown wash and faint streaks on the breast sides and flanks; dark tail with pale brown central feathers and white outer edges; short grey-black bill; dark eye; blackish legs.
art.pose: walking on bare sandy ground, side view, picking at seeds
art.scene: bare sandy coastal dune and fallow field edge in Korea in winter, dry grass and low winter sun; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male in winter, side view walking on bare ground: rounded head, yellow forehead, supercilium, chin and throat, black forecrown band with two small black horn tufts at the sides, black mask from the lores down onto the cheek, black upper-breast band, streaked grey-brown back, whitish underparts, short fine dark bill

adult female in winter, side view walking on bare ground: same slim shape but duller, paler face, less black on the head, narrower black breast band, horn tufts barely visible, streaked grey-brown upperparts, whitish underparts
art.build: A small, slim ground lark, a little longer than a sparrow and slightly smaller than a Eurasian Skylark, with a rather horizontal stance; it walks rather than hops on bare ground. Rounded head with no crest; the 'horns' are only two small black tufts at the rear of the crown, often flattened. Bill short, fine and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs short, blackish. Tail medium, slightly notched. In flight the blackish tail with pale centre contrasts with the pale sandy body and plain sandy upperwing.
avoid: Do not give it a raised crest or a heavily streaked breast; that is Eurasian Skylark (Alauda arvensis).
Do not paint long, ear-like horns; they are two short black tufts, often barely visible in winter.
Do not omit the black mask and black breast crescent; they stay visible in winter, only partly veiled by pale fringes.
Do not make the bill thick or pale; it is short, fine and dark.
Do not paint a white face; birds wintering in Korea have a pale yellow forehead, supercilium and throat.
